scope: Proposition B.7 (Geometric bag extraction) of the manuscript “The strong thin tree conjecture” (preprints/The-strong-thin-tree-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 174 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a2b847ce72f66109), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let T be a nonempty finite set of α-bad nodes with positive boundary sums, where 0 < α ≤ 1. Define J = 1 + ⌈log2(256/α2 )⌉, C2(α) = 128J4 , s = α/C2(α), L = 2 + ⌈log2(1/s)⌉, H = 1 + ⌈log2(24/(λs2 ))⌉, C1(ϵ) = 1024ϵ−2 . Suppose β > 1, 0 < ϵ < 1/3, 0 < λ < 1, and sϵ ≤ (48βC1(ϵ))−1. There is a λ-geometric sequence of families, consisting either entirely of β-compact bags or entirely of s1+2ϵ-assigned bags assigned to distinct nodes of T, whose mass satisfies (B.28) 𝖬 ≥ sϵ 384βC1(ϵ)C2(α)LH ∑ t∈T 1 |O(t)| ⎛ ⎝ ∑ e∈O(t) ae ⎞ ⎠ 2 . In particular, all losses are functions of α, ϵ, β and λ, independent of the number of vertices and hierarchy depth.
